chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Hatam narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salama ibn Abdullah al-Naysaburi narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Mansur, from Mubashir ibn Abdullah ibn Razin, from Sufyan ibn al-Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Amr ibn Ashwa', from Amir al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samura al-Saw'i, who said: I was with my father in the mosque while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was delivering a sermon. I heard him say: 'After me, there will be twelve leaders.' Then he lowered his voice, so I did not know what he said. I asked my father: 'What did he (peace be upon him and his family) say?' He said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of his successors?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the Twelve Imams, with Jabir ibn Samura’s account providing early attestation of their number and Qurayshi lineage. The specific detail that all twelve are from Quraysh reinforces the concept of *Nass* (divine designation) within the Prophet's tribe, a key criterion in Shia political theology for legitimate succession.
